ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Power, CardRarity.Uncommon, TargetType.Self)` (Prowess.cs:26-29) == cost 1 / POWER / UNCOMMON / SELF.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new PowerVar<StrengthPower>(1m)` + `new PowerVar<DexterityPower>(1m)` (Prowess.cs:20-24) are TWO separate vars in C#; the sim collapses them into one `_power_amount`. Safe here and only here: both start at 1 and OnUpgrade raises BOTH by 1 (Prowess.cs:39-40), so the two values are identical at every upgrade level, and `magic_number` reports the shared 1 (then 2). Recorded because the collapse would silently break if a future balance change upgraded them by different amounts -- contrast card/relax, which keeps three separate vars for exactly that reason.

OnPlay.rationale: Both amounts and the Strength-then-Dexterity order match (Prowess.cs:33-34). The divergence is the verb for the FIRST half: C# calls `PowerCmd.Apply<StrengthPower>` while the sim calls `StrengthCmd.apply`, which runs `hooks.modify_strength_given` before `PowerCmd.apply` (cmds.py:349-361); the Dexterity half correctly uses `PowerCmd.apply` directly. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/inflame's OnPlay entry and card/fight_me's guard (rule 3): the sim's `StrengthCmd` is a documented re-architecture of C#'s `Hook.ModifyPowerAmountGiven` / `...Received` chain, which `PowerCmd.Apply` runs anyway (PowerCmd.cs:120-125), so the observable Strength gained is the same. It becomes a gap if a ported `modify_strength_given` listener diverges from the general power-amount modifiers -- and note that would then make Strength and Dexterity behave asymmetrically on THIS card, which is the clearest way to spot it.

OnUpgrade.rationale: `DynamicVars.Dexterity.UpgradeValueBy(1m)` + `DynamicVars.Strength.UpgradeValueBy(1m)` (Prowess.cs:39-40) == `self._power_amount += 1`, which raises both to 2. Note C# upgrades DEXTERITY first; order is irrelevant since they are independent vars.
